items.title: Karnataka High Court denies relief to man whose minor son crashed car killing three
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently refused to quash a criminal charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder against a man whose 14-year-old son allegedly drove a car that killed three members of a family [ Nadeem Ur Rehman Vs State of Karnataka ]. Justice M Nagaprasanna observed that a parent who knowingly allows a minor to drive cannot automatically escape criminal liability when the act ends in tragedy. The Court held that the prosecution must be allowed to proceed against accused man, Nadeem Ur Rehman, as the chargesheet contained prima facie material indicating that he had handed over the car keys to his minor son and permitted him to drive. "A parent who knowingly places the steering wheel in the hands of a child cannot always retreat behind the minority of that child, when the adventure ends in catastrophe. Parenthood carries not merely affection and authority, but responsibility. Roads are shared public spaces, not training grounds for unlawful indulgence," the Court held.
